summary: CC preprocessor's #define body loop read the first token of the next line to detect end-of-body and silently discarded it (no token pushback in the lexer).
evidence: the `#define` body-reading loop consumes the *next* line's first token to detect the boundary, then silently discards it

summary: CC parser read array bounds and enum values as a single literal token, but the codebase's macro constants expand to arithmetic expressions like (1 + 1).
evidence: array bounds in this codebase include computed macro constants (e.g. `TINYFS_INODE_BLOCK` expands to `(1 + 1)`, not a single literal)

summary: A comment in CC's parser.c contained '/*' inside a comment, triggering a -Wcomment build warning.
evidence: parser.c:176:14: warning: ‘/*’ within comment [-Wcomment]

summary: CC preprocessor only accepted #include "file" and rejected angle-bracket header names like #include <stdint.h>.
evidence: cc: tests/toolchain/t01_basic.c:1: expected "file" after #include

summary: AS parse_mem handled [reg+disp] but not [reg-disp], so 'mov dword [ebp-4], 6' failed to assemble.

summary: AS encode_rm32 had no case for a general-register base like [ebx]; it fell through to the bare-label disp32-direct encoding and silently corrupted the address.
evidence: `encode_rm32` had no case for a general register base (like `[ebx]`); it fell through to the "bare label, disp32-direct" branch, silently corrupting the address

summary: CC codegen's compound assignment kept &a in a register that was clobbered (idiv/cdq) while computing the new value (ordering bug).
evidence: ordering bug in compound-assign ... a register copy of it wouldn't survive an idiv/cdq

summary: CC codegen emitted an xchg instruction that AS does not support.
evidence: unnecessary `xchg` that AS doesn't support

summary: CC codegen_emit's loop declaring externs for called-but-undefined functions was broken, and string literals were never emitted.
evidence: broken extern-declaration loop, missing string-literal emission

summary: CC's walk_collect emitted string-literal bytes immediately during the extern-collection pass, before any section directive, corrupting the assembly output.
evidence: `walk_collect` emits string-literal bytes immediately during the extern-collection pass, before any `section` directive exists, corrupting the output

summary: CC codegen's local ND_VAR_DECL handling used a goto into another branch and the for-init handling did not walk multiple declarators.
evidence: fragile `for`-init handling ... Now the `ND_VAR_DECL` goto mess and `ND_FOR` init handling

summary: CC host-target _start code was emitted after the .rodata section switch, so it would land in .rodata instead of .text.
evidence: the `_start` code for host target got placed after the `.rodata` section switch, so it would land in `.rodata` instead of `.text`

summary: CC's __builtin_outb codegen contained dead scratch code.
evidence: That `__builtin_outb`/`__builtin_gdt_flush` code is genuinely broken (dead scratch code, and a hardcoded label that would collide on repeated calls)

summary: CC's __builtin_gdt_flush emitted a hardcoded label that would collide if the builtin was used more than once.
evidence: a hardcoded label that would collide on repeated calls

summary: CC codegen.c used va_start/va_end without including <stdarg.h>, so it failed to compile.
evidence: codegen.c:28:5: error: implicit declaration of function ‘va_start’

summary: AS ELF writer set a symbol's st_shndx to 1 + section_kind instead of the actual ELF section index, so .bss symbols pointed at the wrong section when .data was absent (segfault at run time).
evidence: symbol `st_shndx` was computed as `1 + section_kind_enum` ... Since this file has no `.data` section, `.bss` actually lands at ELF section index 2, not 3

summary: CC computed struct member offsets lazily in type_size(), which nothing called at definition time, so ./-> accesses used offset 0 for every member.
evidence: FAIL t05_structs: expected 17, got 15 ... struct member offsets are computed lazily inside `type_size()`, but nothing calls `type_size()` at struct-definition time

summary: run_toolchain_tests.sh had no expected exit code for the t02_types fixture, so it was silently skipped and never executed.
evidence: SKIP t02_types (no expected value registered)

summary: CC ignored the static storage class on functions and emitted every function as global.

summary: CC preprocessor's resolve_include used snprintf into a fixed buffer, causing a format-truncation warning in the -O2 build.
